chunks: Usul al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm who said:
I heard al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying: The friend of every man is his intellect, and his enemy is his ignorance.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: al-Ridha (the pleased one, a title for Imam Ali al-Ridha)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between intellect and ignorance according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) identifies intellect ('aql) as the innate ally and ignorance (jahln) as the inherent adversary, reflecting the Shia epistemological view that true guidance stems from internal cognitive clarity rather than external authority alone. This maxim underscores the ethical imperative of cultivating self-awareness to align one’s actions with divine reason, a concept central to the Usuli school's emphasis on the intellect as a primary source of law and knowledge.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/2] Usul al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Ibn Fadhal from al-Hasan b. Jahm who said:
I heard al-Ridha عليه السلام saying: the friend of every man is his intellect, and his enemy is his ignorance.
